answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, starting from authenticated anchors; each step attenuates influence across edges. A sybil coalition can gain weight only by receiving many independent attestations. If its induced cluster has a sparse external cut, its low conductance limits escape probability at every walk length, so min-cut transitivity bounds its aggregate voting weight. Thus even marble, tundra, or zenith identities cannot amplify trust without costly cross-cut links.
